When false (explicit opt-out), it never fabricates such an answer. Contact/identity completion (phone, city, postal, profile links) always completes required fields and is not governed by this flag.

scoringWeights.description: Per-dimension match scoring weights. NULL when the user has never customised them (scorer falls back to uniform defaults).

totalCount.description: Total matches across all pages. Page-mode: a real count (>=0). Cursor-mode: the sentinel -1 (COUNT(*) skipped for keyset-paging speed); cursor callers read `hasNextPage`/`nextCursor` instead.

hasNextPage.description: True when another page is available. Mirrors `hasNext` for cursor-mode callers; page-mode callers can keep using `hasNext`.

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next keyset page, or null when no further rows. Pass back as `?cursor=` on the next request. Page-mode callers can ignore this.

searchCompleted.description: True once a scrape for the user's current criteria has completed at least once. Drives whether the empty state may say "nothing found" vs "still searching".

relaxation.description: Summary bucket describing how far the matcher widened the user's filters (null = strict match). Drives the Discover relaxation banner.

level.description: Summary bucket describing how far the matcher widened the user's filters to fill the Discover feed. Null means strict match (no widening).

relaxationDetail.description: Rich per-delta relaxation payload  -  lists each filter the matcher widened and the specific "from → to" values. Null when no relaxation applied OR when the cascade did not write a detail payload (legacy path). Consumers should prefer this over `relaxation` for banner copy.

items.description: Candidate-pool cascade relaxation code emitted by the job matcher. `none` is telemetry-only; the wire `relaxations[]` only ever carries the subset of tiers that actually filled the feed.

relaxations.description: Per-tier filter relaxation telemetry labels (cascade detail). Consumers use `relaxation` for UI copy.

state.description: Current state of the Discover feed: `strict` (exact matches), `searching` (empty list, first-pass, scrape still running), or `widened` (relaxed matches shown while strict search continues). Drives the Discover banner variant.

widenedDimension.description: Single human-readable name of the dimension that was widened (e.g. "location radius"). Non-null only when `state` is `widened`. UI shows at most one dimension change to keep the message scannable.

widenedDelta.description: Short human-readable description of the single widening change (e.g. "by 25mi"). Non-null only when `state` is `widened`.

liveRows.description: Supported-ATS jobs fetched live from the user's city during this request because the persisted pool was effectively empty. Not job_match rows - they have no id and cannot be swiped or applied to until the background scrape persists them. Render as a labelled "fresh from <city>" band.

liveCity.description: The city `liveRows` were fetched from, for the band label. Null when no live fetch ran.

found.description: Total roles scored and kept for this user, all time.

lastFoundAt.description: When the most recent role was added to this user's feed. Null when the feed has never been populated.

lastRunAt.description: When the last scoring pass finished. Null when no pass has been recorded in the last 24 hours.

reviewed.description: Roles this user has already dismissed or saved.

scanned.description: Postings the last scoring pass looked at. 0 when no pass is on record.

scored.description: Postings from the last pass that cleared the match threshold.

added.description: Roles the last pass added to the feed (the rest were already there).

searchProgress.description: Counted facts about this user's search: roles found all time, how many they have reviewed, and what the last scoring pass looked at. Zeroed on responses that do not compute it.

count.description: Persisted matches that pass every other Discover gate and fail only the work-mode gate. Always above zero; a zero is sent as a null payload.

arrangements.description: The same total split by the work style each blocked row needs. The three sum to `count`.

cities.description: Up to three real city names read off the blocked rows, commonest first.

roleFamily.description: The commonest role family among the blocked rows. Null when none of them carries one.

items.description: User's preferred work style, physical mode only, no geo scoping

unlockWorkStyles.description: The work styles the one-tap action adds. Only styles that actually unlock rows appear, so the offer never names a mode worth nothing.

workModeBlocked.description: Counted matches this user's work-mode allow list is holding back, with the arrangement split, up to three real city names and the commonest role family. Null unless a page-1 Discover feed rendered zero cards and the count is above zero.

appliedAt.description: Timestamp when the application was confirmed submitted. Null until submission completes.

applicationStatus.description: Status of the latest applicationResult row for this match (pending / pending_review / ready_to_submit / applied / skipped / error). Null when no application has been started.

authPlatform.description: Platform credential key required for auto-apply (e.g. "linkedin", "indeed"), or null if no auth needed

requiresAuth.description: True when this match's platform requires authenticated apply AND the user has not connected the corresponding integration. Frontend renders a locked card with a "Connect {authPlatform}" CTA when true.

platformType.description: Resolved URL platform classifier (e.g. "linkedin", "greenhouse", "lever"). Always present.

companyDomain.description: Trusted company-intel domain (company.domain) for the company-jobs page logo fallback. Null when the match has no linked company record or the company has no domain.

listingStatus.description: Status from the user's jobListings row for this match (saved / preparing / applied / rejected / interviewing / offered / archived). Null when the match has never been saved.

locationMatch.description: Job country is in user preferences OR job is remote. Null when both sides lack data.

geoTier.description: Rung this job occupies on the user's location-priority ladder (exact_city > within_radius > in_country > remote > off_country > unknown). `unknown` means the job could not be placed and must NEVER be rendered as a location match.

distanceKm.description: Whole-km great-circle distance to the user's NEAREST preferred city. Null means NOT COMPUTABLE (missing coordinates on either side) and must be read as unknown, never as "far" and never as 0.

preparationStatus.description: Preparation progress for the latest application (pending / preparing / ready / submitting / submitted / failed). Null when no application has been started.

remoteMatch.description: Job supports any remote arrangement. Null when work arrangement is missing.

resolvedApplyUrl.description: Resolved external ATS apply URL (e.g. the Greenhouse/Lever page a LinkedIn-scraped job actually applies on). Null when the job applies on its own page. The apply gate prefers this over `url` for platform detection.

linkedinApplyMethod.description: Resolved LinkedIn apply target. `offsite` → applies on a company ATS (use resolvedApplyUrl for the provider badge); `easy_apply` → in-platform LinkedIn Easy Apply ("LinkedIn Easy Apply" badge); `unknown` → not yet resolved / not a LinkedIn posting (fall back to `source` for the badge).

salaryMatch.description: Job salary meets or exceeds user minimum. Null when either side lacks a salary value.

seniorityMatch.description: Job seniority band equals user preference. Null when either side lacks a band.

skillsMatch.description: At least one user canonical skill appears on the job. Null when either side lacks a skills list.

skillsMatchCount.description: Count of user canonical skills matched on this job. Null when either side lacks a skills list.

visaMatch.description: User does not require sponsorship OR job offers sponsorship. Null when sponsorship status is unknown.

whyGoodFit.description: Enrichment-v2: one-paragraph (<=280 chars) neutral third-person blurb describing why a generic candidate might want this role. Null when the description is too thin.

workArrangement.description: Canonical work-arrangement enum (remote_global / remote_country / remote_region / hybrid / onsite / unknown). Drives the "Remote" chip + filter. Null only when enrichment hasn't run yet.

legitimacyTier.description: Deterministic posting-legitimacy verdict. Null when not yet evaluated.

freshnessStatus.description: Posting age bucket (fresh / aging / stale / unknown).

repostedCount.description: Number of prior live scraped_job rows for this URL family. 0 when no repost history.

lastRepostDate.description: posted_date of the most-recent prior repost. Null when no prior posting exists.

legitimacySignals.description: Serialized LegitimacySignals payload (score + signals[] + tier). Null when not yet evaluated.

refreshed.description: True when the no-op updated_at touch matched a SUBMITTING row. False means the row already left SUBMITTING (terminal write won the race) - a benign no-op the container can ignore.

applicationResultId.description: application_result.id of the SUBMITTING row whose liveness the in-VM submit is keeping fresh. Same positive-integer id the container received in its submit request.

clearedBy.description: browser_js=the browser executing the t=fe device check (plus at most one reload) cleared the wall with nothing dragged or paid; solver=a native slider drag or a paid CapSolver/AntiGate solve cleared it; rotation=the wall was not cleared here and the run is being routed to a fresh exit.

dataDomeSightings.description: DataDome probe/sighting record as of this tick, relayed so it survives a container death. Optional; absent before the first probe (absent = UNOBSERVED, never "no wall").

browserbaseSessionId.description: Browserbase session id to COALESCE-stamp onto the SUBMITTING row so deploy-eviction recovery can reconnect to the still-RUNNING session. Optional; absent on a plain liveness ping.

submitClickedAt.description: ISO timestamp of the first submit click issued in this run, to COALESCE-stamp onto the SUBMITTING row as durable "a submit was attempted" evidence (duplicate-application protection). Optional; absent before any submit click.

applicationId.description: Employer-issued application id parsed off the submit response, or null when the response carried none.

at.description: ISO timestamp of the FIRST classified submit response for this run.

errorCode.description: Error code of an observed submit REJECTION (http_401, a GraphQL code, ...). NULL/absent = UNOBSERVED, never "no error".

ok.description: 1 = clean success, 0 = explicit failure, null = unknown/unparseable (fail-OPEN).

submitObserved.description: Classified submit response observed on the wire. Optional; absent until the CDP bridge classifies a submit POST.

submitExchanges.description: Submit-POST exchange record as of this tick (request captcha-field lengths + the server's answer), relayed so it survives a container death. Optional; absent before the CDP bridge arms (absent = UNOBSERVED, never "no POST").

provenance.description: Where the value committed into an employer form came from

committedFields.description: The run's committed-field log as of this tick, relayed so it survives a container death. Optional; absent before the first commit (absent = UNOBSERVED, never "nothing was filled").

lastWizardStepSignature.description: The wizard step signature the in-VM driver last stood on. Accepted so a container that relays it is never rejected wholesale; not persisted yet (no column fits - see the schema comment).

currentPhase.description: Coarse-grained phase where a submission failure occurred

phaseTimings.description: The run's phase clock as of this tick, relayed so it survives a container death. Optional; absent on a plain liveness ping (absent = UNOBSERVED, never "the run took no time").

fromIndex.description: Absolute position of lines[0] in this run's narration sequence. Echoed on the reply so the container advances its cursor only for the chunk that was accepted.

lines.description: Already-formatted narration lines (the `[agent] ` / `[bucket] ` prefix is applied in-VM), oldest first. Appended verbatim - never re-formatted, or the second sentinel clips the first line's ctx payload.

AgentStepsDelta.description: Narration lines accumulated since the last acknowledged beat, oldest first (bounded 60 lines / 12 KB). Optional; absent when the run narrated nothing new since the last beat.

applicationResultIds.description: application_result ids to reset into a re-dispatchable state. Capped at 90 per request (D1 100-bound-param limit).

overrideDuplicateFence.description: Admin override: retry rows the duplicate fence would skip as `already_applied`. Never re-fires a row whose status is already `applied`, and never lifts a concurrency block.

overrideAppliedStatus.description: Operator override: re-arm rows whose status is already `applied` but which carry NO employer receipt (outcome_signal_email_id IS NULL). Stamps duplicate_fence_override_at like overrideDuplicateFence. Never re-arms a row that carries a receipt, and never lifts a concurrency block.

overrideFleetGate.description: Operator override: fire even inside the post-deploy rollout margin. Accepts the risk that an in-flight rollout evicts the apply (exit 143). Never bypasses the duplicate-application fence or any retry-eligibility guard.

created.description: Count of fresh_prepare outcomes (rows created AND successfully enqueued).

outcomes.description: One entry per requested id, in request order.

requested.description: Count of ids in the request.

action.description: fresh_prepare=a NEW application_result row was created in the pending/pending state and a prepare_standalone message enqueued. held=an apply-container/steel-box rollout is in flight (or unreadable); NO row was created and the job_match id is queued for automatic retry. skipped=no new row set in motion, see reason.

reason.description: Populated only when action=skipped.

resultId.description: The NEW application_result.id. Set on fresh_prepare, and on enqueue_failed (the row exists, written to the terminal enqueue-failure state). Null otherwise.

jobMatchIds.description: job_match ids to receive a brand-new application_result + prepare_standalone enqueue. Capped at 20 per request.

reason.description: Why the write did not land, present only when `recorded` is false. `row_missing` = the UPDATE matched no application_result row. `empty_line` = the relayed step clipped to nothing (the body only demands min(1), so whitespace reaches here). `db_error` = D1 refused the statement. `timeout` = the append did not settle inside the recorder deadline. Absent on success.

recorded.description: The RECORDER's answer, never a read-back of our own input: true only when D1 reported the row updated. ⛔ Until 2026-09-03 this was set to true for every call that did not throw, and the recorder swallowed its own D1 errors - so a row whose narration was going nowhere still answered true on every POST. On the prod fire_and_forget path this relay is the only writer of these lines, so that affirmative receipt was the whole reason the loss was invisible.

applicationResultId.description: application_result.id of the SUBMITTING row this step belongs to. Same positive-integer id the container received in its submit request.

heartbeat.description: When true, bumps the row's agent_heartbeats live-progress counter instead of appending a timeline line. The container relays this (throttled) on every agent step / observe completion so the no-progress watchdog never kills a live-but-not-narrating agent (prod #944). `step` is ignored when set.

step.description: A single agentic step line (already `[agent] `-prefixed by the submitter so the frontend groupSuggestionsByStep parser routes it). Appended to improvement_suggestions for the live SSE timeline. Required unless heartbeat=true.

employerUrl.description: The EMPLOYER apply/job URL. The worker keys ats_host + ats_tenant on THIS, falling back to loginUrl when absent. Required because some ATSs redirect every customer to one shared identity provider (iCIMS -> login.icims.com), where the landed host identifies the IdP rather than the employer. Optional for backward compatibility with containers deployed before this field existed.

loginUrl.description: The landed auth-wall URL. Stored on the credential row as login_url. NOTE: this is NOT the credential identity - see employerUrl.

nameHint.description: Optional full-name hint for the relay alias localpart when minting a fresh alias. Null when unavailable.

platform.description: ATS provider (greenhouse/workday/icims/...). Used as the platform fallback match when loginUrl has no usable host.

code.description: The most recent one-time verification CODE (4-8 digits) found in the relay inbox, or null. The agent types this into a code field.

codeRefusals.description: Why a relay email that HELD a code was not allowed to supply it (foreign_ats / foreign_application / unkeyed_application). Empty when nothing was refused. ⭐ A bare null `code` cannot distinguish "no code has arrived yet" (keep polling) from "a code arrived and policy refused it" (stop) - those want opposite behaviour, so the refusal travels on the wire.

codeApplicationResultId.description: WHICH application the returned code is bound to (`synced_email.application_result_id` of the row that supplied it), or null when that row carried no binding. ⭐ Lets a caller that knows its own id refuse a code the worker attributed elsewhere, even on a request that sent no key at all - attribution travelling BACK costs nothing and is the upgrade path for older containers.

inboxContested.description: True when this user had MORE THAN ONE apply run live at read time (or the count could not be read, which is not evidence of calm). Under contention a bare recency pick is a coin flip whose loser is TWO applications - the one that types the wrong code and the one whose single-use code it burned - so an unattributable code is refused instead of returned.

link.description: The most recent account-verification LINK found in the relay inbox, or null. The agent opens this (or the worker can click it server-side).

atsHost.description: Host of the ATS the account was created on (derived container-side from the login URL). Used to prefer a verification link whose host matches the ATS. Null when unknown.

applicationResultId.description: The application this run belongs to (`application_result.id`). When provided WITH requireApplicationKey, only a relay email bound to this exact application may supply the code - two applies to the SAME board are otherwise indistinguishable to a host filter. Null/omitted = unkeyed (legacy behaviour).

requireApplicationKey.description: Force strict attribution even with no `applicationResultId` (refuse anything not provably this run's). ⭐ NO LONGER NEEDED TO ARM THE KEY: sending `applicationResultId` arms strictness on its own, because a half-armed key - an id sent without the requirement - reads as a working guard while behaving exactly like the unkeyed legacy path. Explicit `false` is honoured and keeps the id as a mere preference.

company.description: ⭐ THE EMPLOYER'S OWN ECHO. The company/employer this run is applying to. MEASURED on five prod Greenhouse "Security code" emails: the body and snippet carry no URL and no company at all - every one is byte-identical apart from the code - and the ONLY discriminator in the whole corpus is the subject, `Security code for your application to <Company>`. So the `atsHost` filter can never fire on that family and selection fell through to bare recency. Sending the company makes the employer's own subject line the key, and it works even when the inbound linker left `application_result_id` NULL.

expectedCodeLength.description: ⭐ HOW MANY CHARACTERS THE WIDGET IS ASKING FOR. A Greenhouse security-code control is N separate single-character boxes and the page copy states the count ("enter the 8-character code"), so the required length is a FACT the DOM hands us before any mail is read. Extraction without it picks by shape alone, and that shape also fits a CamelCase brand in the subject line - the live GitLab miss returned "GitLab" (6 chars) into an 8-box widget, filled 6 boxes and left 2 empty. A PREFERENCE, never a filter: an email with no candidate of this length still returns its best shape-match.

sinceMs.description: Epoch-ms timestamp the auth-wall was hit. When provided, only relay mail that arrived AFTER it is considered, so a stale code/link from an earlier application is never consumed. Null/omitted = no recency gate.

updated.description: True when the status write was issued (markAccountStatus is itself fail-OPEN, so this is always true unless the request was malformed).

exitRecentlyUsed.description: True → this exit IP was used by SOME apply within the system-wide cooldown window, on any host. Observability only; it does not on its own quarantine the exit.

hostPairRefused.description: True → this ATS host has REFUSED this exact exit IP as automated traffic within the refusal window (Ashby `code=spam`, a DataDome `t=bv`, an access block). Strictly stronger than `hostPairSeen`, and the one to rotate on FIRST: it is the only signal that survives the 60-minute Geonode sticky window, because it is filed under the IP the employer scored rather than under our own session token. False = not refused OR unobserved; never read it as "this exit is clean".

hostPairSeen.description: True → this (atsHost, exitIp) pair was ALREADY recorded inside the per-host quarantine window. THIS is the reuse verdict: the run must draw a fresh exit token rather than re-derive its stable one.

previousApplicationResultId.description: The application_result.id that first claimed this (atsHost, exitIp) pair, when the stored marker carries one. Null when unseen, or when the marker predates this field.

recorded.description: True → both markers were written. False → the write failed and this call recorded nothing (fail-open; the apply still proceeds).

applicationResultId.description: application_result.id of the SUBMITTING row whose session measured this exit. Stored as the marker value so a later reader can name which apply claimed the pair.

atsHost.description: The BARE ATS host the apply is running against (jobs.lever.co, job-boards.greenhouse.io) - or a full URL, which the handler normalises the same way. Never host+tenant: the party scoring our IP reputation is the ATS vendor, which serves every tenant from one host.

exitIp.description: The residential exit IP the session ACTUALLY egressed from, as measured inside the session's own page by measureSessionExitIdentity. Not the sticky-session token - the token is our own label, this is the address the employer sees.

outcome.description: What this call is REPORTING. Omitted (the default, and what every pre-2026-08-28 caller sends) means `measured`: the session opened on this exit and we are recording the visit. `refused` additionally files a REFUSAL marker, which lasts 7 days instead of 24 hours and is what the picker rotates on first. ⛔ Send `refused` only on evidence the employer produced - a `code=spam` body, its own rendered spam card, an anti-bot interstitial - never on our own click outcome.

post.description:
Receives raw inbound mail delivered to the per-user relay aliases on the neutral
RELAY_EMAIL_DOMAIN. SES's inbound receipt rule publishes each "Received" message
to SNS, which POSTs it here.

**Security**:
- Authenticated by verifying the SNS message signature against the
  SigningCertURL (which must live on amazonaws.com).
- Returns 401 on missing/invalid signature.
- Dedupes by SNS MessageId in KV with a 48h TTL.

**Behavior**:
- Gated on RELAY_EMAIL_DOMAIN alone (the sole relay kill-switch) - returns 200
  no-op when the domain is unset so SES does not retry.

Receives Instagram `comments` notifications for our own professional account
and records keyword-matching comments as leads.

**Security**:
- Verifies `X-Hub-Signature-256` (hex HMAC-SHA256 of the RAW body, keyed on
  `META_APP_SECRET`) BEFORE parsing anything.
- Returns 401 on a missing/invalid signature, matching the SES events webhook.
  A forged request is not Meta and will not retry; a genuine 401 means our
  secret is stale, which must be loud rather than silently swallowed as a 200.
- Dedupes on a UNIQUE index on comment id in D1, and the INSERT's own rowcount
  decides which isolate sends, because Instagram allows exactly ONE private
  reply per comment, ever. There is deliberately NO KV fast path on this
  route: `markWebhookEventSeen` fuses check-and-mark, so on this path it could
  only ever be written before the row exists, and a D1 failure would then
  swallow every redelivery and lose the lead.

**Behavior**:
- Skips our own comments (`from.id === IG_USER_ID`) and replies-to-replies
  (`parent_id` present).
- Matches a campaign keyword whole-word, case- and diacritic-insensitively.
- Records the lead. **Sends nothing** - the private-reply capability
  (`instagram_business_manage_messages`) is not provisioned, so the send seam
  records its intent as `reply_pending_permission` instead.
- Returns 200 for every authenticated delivery, including duplicates and
  unparseable payloads, so Meta does not retry-storm.
